title: One sample suffices for matroid prophet inequalities
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that one independent sample per element suffices for a constant-competitive prophet inequality on every finite matroid: a fixed online rule earns at least 2^(-293) times the expected optimum, even when the arrival order is chosen by an adversary who sees all samples, all values and the rule's random seed. The first lesson proves the matroid facts used, the optimality of greedy, states the theorem and reduces it to a hidden fixed weight vector with sacrificed revealed labels. The second rounds weights to powers of 2^32, gives a maximum rule, and defines four random masks and the candidate labels. The third builds density expansions, nominal and guarded paths of flats, and a generator budget for a whole path. The fourth gives the layered online decisions, their feasibility, a rank bound valid for every order, and a telescoping cost of later path enlargements. The fifth proves a bound on disjoint certificates of an increasing event under adaptive reads. The sixth exposes guard bits backwards in auxiliary time and shows that many revealed labels are safe from lighter competitors. The seventh counts pivot-mark vectors after insertions into a marked sequence via sign patterns of affine functions. The eighth turns safe samples into rank among unrevealed labels by a union bound over a small family of residuals. The ninth thins by the test mask, sums over weight levels, proves the constant, and derives a secretary rule with an adversarial suffix.
prerequisites: finite sets, independence of finitely many random variables and conditional expectation over finite probability spaces; random values with arbitrary laws on [0, infinity) enter only through expectations of nonnegative measurable functions
the course proves all matroid facts it uses

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch pp_checks.py, output pp_checks.out, 10 Oct 2026, 70,514 checks of 53 kinds, 0 problems) on random linear matroids over GF(2) with 4 to 10 labels, loops included. The deterministic lemmas hold for all values of the constants and were tested with kappa in {1/2, 1, 2} and mask rates 0.3 to 0.4 on 193 random instances: submodularity and closure; greedy over a base and greedy optimality (against brute force); largest maximizers, monotonicity, idempotence and the residual bound of density expansions; all path properties and nominal births; the generator budget with insertion times; feasibility of the online rule for every prefix of 25 random orders per instance; the order-uniform rank bound in every tested order; the telescoping rank cost; K inside the lighter guarded path; witness counts, residual inside the revealed masks, and sigma <= kappa z + |R|; the two marked sequences of the eighth lesson (first marks = valid births, spans after each part of each layer, residual = intersection of mark-1 sets); the reverse map reproducing the paths, outputs inside the later state, and the hybrid containment. Exact enumeration: candidate mass E u(Y) = W/2 and E u(U) = E u(greedy on H) <= W over all masks H, and the maximum-rule bound (60 matroids); monotone exit probabilities and the double-exit identity Pr = p^2 at 62 reverse steps (equal guard and test rates; with unequal rates the identity fails, as the proof requires equal rates); the certificate bound for 400 random increasing events and adaptive procedures; pivot-mark vectors over all insertions (80 cases) against 4^s sum C(n,l). Constants: 2^(-11)(14 log 2 + 1) < 1/2 and the band-sum identity, the family-size constant, the error constant below 2^(-21), gamma/4 - 2^(-21) >= gamma/8, the transfer constant, and the subset-count bound.
